text: Today, I will explain how we intend to do so, in three areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we want to strengthen our Built Environment sector and transform the way we design, build and maintain our city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we seek to design a new HDB housing model, to ensure that prime areas of our city remain diverse and inclusive for Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And finally, we want to pursue our goal of a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleagues will thereafter cover other areas of MND's core work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Together, these are among MND's key priorities for this term of Government, as we set out in our Addendum to the President's Address, at the opening of Parliament last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The sector was hit very hard by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the circuit breaker period, most construction work was suspended and many companies struggled.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Even when projects could resume, the challenges mounted – ensuring the health of our foreign workers, implementing safe management measures and so on.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There was tremendous uncertainty and a lot of coordination and daily adjustments were needed on the ground, as the situation kept evolving.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, in the early days of this crisis, we had literally daily meetings with our partners and our trade associations every day to adjust, to understand what was going on and to work together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through it all, the Government had worked with firms to help them tide over these difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In response to industry feedback, we are working with the Singapore Contractors Association Ltd (or SCAL) and other trade associations and chambers (TACs) to facilitate claims for prolongation costs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also extended the Project Completion Period and the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty remission timelines, to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on developers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, we provided protection to purchasers from developers, in cases where the purchasers had difficulties making their contractual payments on time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But with the perseverance of our companies and Government agencies and partners, we will ride through this together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to monitor industry demand closely, given the uncertainties of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also recognise that the industry still faces serious challenges even though works have resumed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Safe management measures on worksites have affected productivity, while restrictions on the inflow of foreign workers have resulted in a labour crunch and higher manpower costs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are aware of these issues and are working closely with our partners and our agencies to address them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, with MOM and MOH, we are reviewing whether the safe management measures on worksites can be adjusted, but we need to balance this against a possible increase in transmission risks onsite – especially since in the last few weeks, we have seen cases again popping up in the construction sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also working with agencies to see how we can ease the tight manpower situation for companies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But above all, this experience has strengthened our resolve to accelerate the pace of change as set out in our Industry Transformation Map and decisively transform the way we design, build and maintain our city, once and for all.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We cannot go back to how we used to do construction in the past.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have heard this conviction echoed more resolutely in many of our conversations with industry partners.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will, therefore, embark on three complementary strategies, to give a stronger push for the sector's transformation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we will enhance Government support to uplift the entire Built Environment value chain.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we will strengthen our regulations to spur productivity growth and reduce reliance on foreign manpower.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And third, we will step up our research and development (R&D) efforts to create and deploy innovative solutions in the Built Environment sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the Built Environment sector, unlike many other sectors, there are heavy inter-dependencies among different stakeholders along the value chain.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Developers work with builders and consultants on each project, who, in turn, rely on multiple tiers of contractors and sub-contractors for different aspects of the project.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given these inter-linkages, it is difficult for any one firm in the value chain to transform on its own.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This value chain approach differs from existing schemes in two important respects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, existing schemes focus on individual projects, which can result in contractors operating at very thin margins to meet short-term targets, without the capacity to invest in long-term transformation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In contrast, the GTS supports firms in improving their capabilities, not just in completing specific projects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The GTS will support the formation of strategic alliances among progressive developers, builders, consultants and sub-contractors across the entire value chain.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It should also seek to achieve sustainability targets, build better capabilities, develop our workforce and improve business growth and strategic collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The alliance members will work together collectively for the outcomes committed to in their business plan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is how the Built Environment sector works on projects and comes together to make transformations happen.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In this way, the value chain approach will help alliance members forge long-term collaboration, reap mutual benefits and build capabilities through knowledge sharing and transfer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help pave the way for the alliances to take on larger or more complex projects or develop niche strengths in the future.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will roll out the GTS with a few alliances first, and learn and improve the scheme along the way.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over time, the GTS should catalyse transformations throughout the Built Environment eco-system, so that the sector can progress together, including our sub-contractors further down the value chain.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With enhanced capabilities and a stronger track record, Singapore firms will also be better placed to compete in construction tenders both here and abroad.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: More details will be announced later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides the Growth and Transformation Scheme, we will also enhance our other broad-based incentives to help firms accelerate their transformation, such as through the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, in tandem, we will strengthen our regulations, to spur greater productivity improvements.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will review our foreign manpower levers in the construction industry.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also studying the reduction of the construction Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC), to support more manpower-lean construction.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are aware that changes in these regulations will impact the construction industry and are especially mindful of the current economic climate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to consult our industry partners before making any major moves.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also be enhancing our Buildability Framework to raise productivity standards and make Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) the default method for large projects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the short term, these moves may cause some pain, as many industry players accept.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But as we have learnt from COVID-19, these structural changes are necessary, so that we can build greater resilience in our industry.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we will be investing more resources to support our local industry’s research and innovation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By developing and deploying transformative technologies, we can spur industry growth and improve our firms’ competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond productivity and resilience, we also want our Built Environment sector to be even more green and sustainable, in line with the Green Plan, and we talked about it earlier during the segment on the Green Plan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague Minister of State Tan Kiat How will elaborate on our plans to transform the Built Environment sector later in greater detail.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Now let me move on to another key priority for us, which is public housing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai expressed concern about possible shortages in housing supply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For public housing, HDB adopts a comprehensive approach in planning new flat supply, taking into account demographic and socio-economic trends, prevailing market conditions and the supply of resale flats on the open market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But our approach to public housing goes beyond matching supply to demand and putting a physical roof over people’s heads.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Public housing is also an integral part of the social fabric that keeps our nation together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It serves important social objectives that are fundamental to the idea of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Unlike almost anywhere else in the world, here in Singapore, we provide public housing for the vast majority of our people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When we live next door to diverse neighbours along the same corridor or in the same estate, we share common experiences and we grow a sense of identity and community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we must do our best to keep public housing diverse and inclusive, to nurture and strengthen this community spirit.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Take the Ethnic Integration Policy, or EIP, for example.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is a unique policy and an intrusive one, almost impossible to replicate elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But as Mr Saktiandi Supaat had emphasised, the EIP remains important to promote social integration, by ensuring a balanced racial mix in our HDB blocks and neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, it is an important strategy, but it works together with other community-building strategies to ensure that our multi-culturalism is never taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, some flat owners may find it more challenging to sell their flats when the EIP limits are met.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members have referred cases to us from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We must take care to ensure that they do not bear a disproportionate share of the EIP’s impact.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many of these owners are eventually able to sell their flats to buyers from eligible ethnic groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But for those who continue to face difficulties, HDB can give them more time to sell their flat, or exercise flexibility on the EIP in truly extenuating circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will look at appeals closely on a case-by-case basis and continue to monitor the situation carefully.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will now talk about how we will keep public housing inclusive, by keeping flats affordable and meeting the diverse needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will then touch on our efforts to streamline processes for home seekers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These subsidies keep flats affordable for most buyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, they can pay their monthly instalments mostly through their CPF contributions, with very little or even no cash outlay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Moving forward, as we have said, we will also build public housing in very prime locations, like the city centre and the Greater Southern Waterfront.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin had asked about these plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Left solely to the private market, these prime areas would likely be used for exclusive, high-end housing developments that only the rich can afford, given their attractive locations and attributes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We see this in many other cities, from New York to Hong Kong and many others, where housing is much more expensive in certain choice neighbourhoods compared to others, and average families either have to pay very high rents to live in these prime locations, or may need to move further out of the city or to less desirable parts of the inner city to buy an affordable home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are very powerful social and economic forces at work, that drive stratification and gentrification of cities, that can divide communities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we are determined to do our best to resist them, so that our society does not become fragmented over time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also design and introduce a whole new housing model to keep new HDB flats that we will build in these prime areas affordable for young families and Singaporeans of different backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will not be easy, as there are many factors to consider.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, to keep flats in these prime areas affordable, our new housing model will have to provide additional subsidies, on top of the generous subsidies that we already provide for BTO flats today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, not just the general subsidies that everyone else gets, but for people who are buying these flats in these very prime locations, to keep it affordable, we have to put additional subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We must also ensure that these future estates remain affordable and inclusive over time and not just at the point when HDB sells to the first buyer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Otherwise, they may transact at extremely high prices in the resale market and only the better-off can buy them over time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In short, as a social policy, we have to act against the instinct of the market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many ideas that have surfaced during our engagements, and there have been lots of commentaries in the media and in professional groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, imposing a longer minimum occupation period, or restrictions on renting out these flats, or ringfencing the pool of subsequent buyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also received many other very good suggestions from experts, commentators, researchers, professionals, sociologists, members of the public and so on, and we welcome people to continue sending in these ideas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But even the authors themselves recognise that these ideas may create complexities too – for instance, they may exacerbate the burden on homeowners who may run into unforeseen circumstances or financial difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And some acknowledge there may be no certainty that some of the measures that are suggested would actually be able to maintain affordability over time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, it is a balancing act, and we are still carefully studying the possibilities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to engage Singaporeans to find the right balance, before announcing more details.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But what I want to stress is that at the heart of our approach is our deep conviction: that our public housing estates must remain inclusive and accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Again, this is a unique approach, that very few other cities would be willing to attempt to do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we are pursuing it, despite the challenges, because we firmly believe that it is right and necessary, to keep Singapore an open and egalitarian society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, we also keep public housing inclusive by meeting the diverse housing needs of different groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In many cases, this goes beyond just providing a form of shelter.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As I said, public housing serves important social objectives.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is also about connecting residents to a wider community – building bonds among them, promoting well-being, building identity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, one group that we take special care of are seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MND, HDB and MOH worked closely to design this new typology, to meet not just the housing needs or shelter needs, but also the social and care needs of seniors, and help them to foster social bonds as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Public feedback on this pilot has been very encouraging, and my colleague, Minister of State Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, will provide a fuller update later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Another group that we look after is our lower income households in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Again, this is not just about basic shelter.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to help them overcome the various complex challenges they face and uplift their lives.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF will elaborate more about this during its COS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the same spirit, we are always looking for ways to better support our public rental households, including single tenants who find it difficult to find a flatmate or to live with one, and larger families with children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Minister of State Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim will share more details about our initiatives for these groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One more group that we take care of is the young couples looking to start their families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao suggested a BTR, not BTO, Build to Rent model.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While Mr Leong Mun Wai suggested letting millennials rent, not buy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are always open to studying different housing typologies, but for now our focus is to help Singaporeans achieve their aspirations of home ownership.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Home ownership gives families a more stable long-term housing arrangement and also, a concrete stake in Singapore’s progress.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why, as I mentioned, we offer generous grants to help young families afford their first flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also provide other assistance, such as by giving them more ballot chances and setting aside more flats for them in HDB’s sales exercises.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After booking a new flat, most families waiting for their flat to be completed continue staying with their families, while some choose to rent on the open market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB also has the Provisional Parenthood Housing Scheme, or PPHS, as Mr Louis Chua pointed out, for those who may need an alternative.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB has been working to add more PPHS flats in recent years and we are studying how we can provide more options for such families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to keep public housing inclusive for other groups as well, such as persons with disabilities or special needs, as Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Denise Phua frequently in this House have highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will share more about our efforts to foster an even stronger sense of community in our HDB estates, by involving Singaporeans in building a caring and vibrant neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think this last year we have achieved in one year a significant acceleration in the digitalisation of many aspects – of the economy, of work and of society, and so, too, we have to keep up.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have made improvements over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, we introduced the HDB Resale Portal in 2018, the open booking of flats in 2019 and the HDB Flat Portal in January this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through our engagements with Singaporeans and with industry, we have planned some new initiatives this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, buyers’ eligibility for these three components is assessed separately.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will streamline these eligibility checks into one online application, made through the HDB Flat Portal.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where possible and with the applicants’ permission, HDB will then link up with other Government agencies backend, to retrieve the details needed for its assessments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This reduces the need for applicants to manually enter their particulars or submit supporting documents repeatedly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This HFE letter will notify applicants of their eligibility to buy a new or resale flat, and how much of an HDB housing loan and CPF housing grants they can qualify for.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This provides upfront clarity and holistic information on their housing and financing options, to facilitate their housing choices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The platform will consolidate all relevant information and present it to buyers at the appropriate milestones.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Because sometimes buying a first flat can be quite daunting – lots of processes, information is here and there.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to align it together, guide them in a family-centric, client-centric way through the process and enable them to book the necessary appointments seamlessly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB will provide more details on these initiatives later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Greening our city has always been a part of Singapore’s DNA, which we must continue to steward for generations to come.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will also help to mitigate the effects of climate change and urbanisation, and improve the living environment for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since we announced our City in Nature vision and goal at COS last year, we have made progress on various initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, as part of our OneMillionTrees movement, we have already planted around 160,000 trees so far.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also launched the new Sungei Buloh Nature Park Network in August last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we announced plans to rewild selected landscapes across our island, to support ecological connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the Joint Segment on the Green Plan, I set out some of our targets.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These include adding another 1,000 hectares of green spaces over the next 10 to 15 years, and expanding our Park Connector Network or PCN so that by 2030, every household will be within a 10-minute walk from a park.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, we have a Coast-to-Coast trail that cuts across central Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also developing the Round Island Route, the Rail Corridor, and the Bukit Timah-Rochor Green Corridor.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will establish and curate more of these recreational routes, so that Singaporeans have more opportunities to enjoy nature and the outdoors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, because of COVID-19, many Singaporeans are now exploring Singapore like never before and it is a wonderful thing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will create two more corridors running from North to South, just like the Rail Corridor.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also create two new Coast-to-Coast trails running from East to West.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the North, we will have a 25-km Coast-to-Coast Northern Trail, running from Khatib Bongsu to Sungei Buloh.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in time to come, as the boy band Westlife put it, you can go from "Coast to Coast" and find the trail you love the most!

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, we will enhance our park connector infrastructure along Phase 1 of the Round Island Route, between Rower’s Bay and Gardens by the Bay, to make it more seamless and accessible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how we can make our park connectors safer for users.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks is focusing on enhancing the safety of park connectors with high usage and more frequent feedback on user conflicts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Enhancement works include segregating wider park connectors into footpaths and cycling paths, updating markings and signage for better clarity, and implementing more lighting, speed regulating strips and advisory signs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Notwithstanding this, there will still be a need for users to share paths, for example where space does not allow for segregation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks conducts regular outreach efforts to raise awareness on park connector etiquette, such as keeping left on shared paths and giving way to others.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, NParks and LTA also conduct joint enforcement against errant park connector users, such as Personal Mobility Device users who exceed the speed limits or ride recklessly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks will continue to work with LTA and the community to promote responsible use of our park connectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These will allow for immersive experiences for all sorts of visitors – from families to hikers and cyclists.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This work will help make Singapore greener, more liveable and more sustainable, and we invite all Singaporeans to join us on this journey.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Building a more resilient Built Environment sector, keeping public housing inclusive and transforming Singapore into a City in Nature – together with the presentations that my colleagues will provide later, these are some of MND’s key priorities in the years ahead and beyond.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are ambitious, meaningful projects, but the Government cannot push them through alone.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need all Singaporeans to take part – individuals, businesses and community organisations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As we continue to build Singapore together, we will need to anticipate long-term social and economic trends and plan for them, while being flexible to adapt to near-term changes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Given our limited land and many pressing needs, including new ones that surface on the horizon, we will also need to make difficult trade-offs across different priorities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are conversations that we need everyone to contribute to, with your different passions and expertise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleague Minister Indranee Rajah who will speak next will explain how we will involve Singaporeans in this very important but very exciting journey.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As the COVID-19 pandemic has shown, we are far stronger when we work as one.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am confident that we can build a more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable Singapore, together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, let me speak today about re-imagining Singapore together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will start with when we were a backwater becoming a global city.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is one of the most liveable cities in the world today, ranking first in Asia under Mercer’s annual Quality of Living Survey, and ahead of cities like London and New York.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Yet, our Pioneers would recall the squatter settlements by the polluted Singapore River and remember that we were once a jumble of urban development and older areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have come a long way since then.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore’s remarkable transformation is not to be taken for granted.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is the fruit of careful and far-sighted urban planning and design.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are now planning for our future city.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Allow me to outline MND’s plans which we will be sharing with the public so that we can reimagine Singapore together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our land is limited yet we have many needs and hopes for the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We want housing options, with amenities at our doorsteps and green spaces to enjoy.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also need to keep Singapore safe and sustainable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Long-term planning is key to achieving these objectives and providing a high quality living environment for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The last major review was conducted in 2011.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With changing needs and emerging trends, it is timely to refresh these plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My colleagues at URA and MND face very different circumstances from our pioneer city planners today.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For a start, as more of Singapore’s land is built up, we must plan not only for development, but also for re-development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Henry Kwek had suggested considering carbon emissions when deciding if we should develop on greenfield or brownfield sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The spirit of this proposal is line with our national push towards sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Yet, there is a tension between this and other considerations that guide our land use plans, including demographic, socio-economic and technological trends.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also have to balance demands across a variety of needs, such as housing, green spaces, schools and so on.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Minister Desmond Lee emphasised, we do our best to optimise our land use, and retain green spaces with high ecological value.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Any decision to develop greenfield sites is taken only after considering trade-offs and alternatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We proceed with care, to minimise the environmental impact.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Overall, taking a long-term approach towards land use planning is important for sustainable development in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will also preserve options for our future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The world that we live in is increasingly volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, our approach to long-term planning will place a greater focus on optionality and flexibility.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As our circumstances change, we must plan accordingly.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes planning for an ageing population and the evolving mindsets of Singaporeans on matters such as lifestyles, work, family, nature and heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, Mr Cheng Hsing Yao asked if we will review our land planning strategies to offer more diverse housing modalities, given our ageing population and decreasing household sizes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Indeed, MND, URA and HDB will continue to monitor societal trends, engage industry stakeholders and adjust land use policies to meet our housing needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong had also suggested to allow more market flexibility in our zoning policies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to review how our land-use policies can keep Singapore resilient and responsive to change and consult stakeholders and businesses in this process.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Prof Hoon Hian Teck and Mr Cheng Hsing Yao also asked if COVID-19 will change our land-use plans and designs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We recognise that it has impacted the way we live, work and play.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, many of us order food and attend meetings with a click of a button, much more so than before COVID-19 hit us last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the national level, COVID-19 has underlined the need for resilience of resources, including food, medical supplies and construction materials.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Last year, in the Emerging Stronger Conversations, a group of Singaporeans and I discussed how to rethink the design of HDB living in light of the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many suggested more community work and study spaces, for those in need of a conducive environment for remote working.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, residents with telecommuting needs can use HDB's "Community Living Rooms" within void decks in new developments, or shared spaces in some of our Community Clubs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those in need of dedicated rooms for videoconferencing can tap on commercial co-working spaces in some of our heartland malls.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will study ways to inject community co-working spaces in our neighbourhoods and explore how to make these accessible for vulnerable groups, as suggested by Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also engage private operators and examine how we can plan for and design our neighbourhoods to support remote working, should the trend persist.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: COVID-19 also raised questions on how much office and retail space we need, considering the shift towards e-commerce and telecommuting.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The disconcerting quiet of the CBD during circuit breaker sharpened the importance of planning for more mixed-use in our city centre.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The CBD Incentive Scheme and Strategic Development Incentive, or SDI scheme, which Mr Louis Chua and Mr Henry Kwek asked about, are well-placed to facilitate this shift.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since 2019, we have offered incentives to encourage the conversion of older office buildings in the CBD into mixed-used developments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These will have offerings, such as hotels, residences, gyms, grocery stores, eateries and so on.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The SDI similarly incentivises building owners to come together to comprehensively redevelop and transform precincts in strategic areas across Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chua also asked if the scheme can be expanded to more areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: URA is actively working with building owners to realise their plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will introduce a good mix of uses and amenities in our city, making it an attractive destination to live, work and play.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to monitor the trends accelerated by COVID-19 and factor these insights into our plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members have also asked if the public and industry will be consulted on our long-term plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We believe that everyone has a stake in building the Singapore that our children and grandchildren will live in.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The LTPR will gather the public, private and people sectors, all of whom bring valuable perspectives and expertise to the table.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Throughout the rest of the year, URA will tap on various platforms to engage Singaporeans deeply and widely.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will use a range of modalities to do so, including polls, workshops and focus group discussions, both in-person and online.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Subsequently, we will gather input on the long-term land-use strategies and plans that can help us achieve these outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given our limited land, difficult conversations on weighing the potential trade-offs and coming to the right balance on land-use decisions will come up.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will not shy away from these conversations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also look forward to ideas on how to shape our major long-term strategic redevelopment areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include the relocation of the Paya Lebar Airbase and the redevelopment of the Greater Southern Waterfront after the ports move to Tuas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At URA's "Runway for your Imagination" competition last year, we received many creative proposals on how to repurpose the former Paya Lebar Airport.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A winning entry envisioned housing an agricultural park at the former runway, supplying fresh produce for the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Green corridors would run through the town, allowing residents to enjoy nature at their doorstep.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was a refreshing vision of a residential town that responded to the global challenges of food resiliency and ecological sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such insights from academia, professional bodies and the public can help us formulate better long-term plans and strategies for Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we gather feedback, debate through options and listen to one other in the coming months, I am confident that we will build consensus on the way forward.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I invite all Singaporeans to spread the word and join us in this process.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we reimagine Singapore, we also want to partner Singaporeans in action.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am heartened by the energy of the Alliances for Actions, or AfAs, launched by the Emerging Stronger Taskforce last year, which some colleagues have already spoken on.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These collaborations allow industry and community to partner the Government to ideate and implement solutions together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The AfA drives the adoption of digital platforms based on industry-wide Common Data Environment Data Standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We hope that more will embrace the collaborative potential of digitalisation across the Built Environment value chain.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes the pilot Business Improvement District or BID programme, in which businesses and stakeholders work with URA to develop and implement business plans that will enhance the vibrancy of our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the thick of the pandemic last year, the Tanjong Pagar stakeholders rallied together to roll out a joint F&B delivery promotion to boost business amid restrictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also thankful for our Friends of the Parks communities, where Singaporeans from all walks of life have stepped forward to promote the active and responsible use of our green spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have started to involve our communities in the conceptualisation, design and development of five of our upcoming parks, including Pasir Panjang Park which will open this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to work with you to create better parks for everyone to enjoy.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, building a City of Tomorrow through innovation and technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our physical resources may be limited, but innovation and technology offer opportunities to overcome this.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Desmond Lee had earlier spoken about MND's Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These research efforts will allow us to tap on innovations in science and technology to transform urban living in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One of these is the creation of "noise-cancelling windows".

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are all familiar with noise feedback from residents living near roads and expressways.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One solution is to create thicker windows to block the noise, but keeping windows closed may lose us the benefit of natural ventilation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The NTU team working on this project will be using noise to cancel out noise.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To do so, their windows will generate sounds of a similar amplitude but of opposite waves – a simple law of physics I am told!

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These cutting-edge urban solutions will allow for a comfortable living environment even as we intensify our land use and establish Singapore as a highly liveable city.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the heart of our plans are our people.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The landscapes and buildings we create are to support the individual and collective dreams of Singaporeans, both present and future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The exciting thing about infrastructure and land use planning is that our plans will come to fruition in very tangible ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The historic districts of Chinatown, Kampong Glam and the Singapore River are legacies of the 1822 Jackson Plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The 1971 Concept Plan laid the blueprint for Changi Airport and our system of expressways and MRT lines which we enjoy today.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The 1991 Concept Plan birthed the idea of connecting parks, green spaces and waterways through a network.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, what imprint would this edition of the Long-Term Planning Review leave behind?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we look to the transformation of Singapore within a generation, may it give us confidence that we have the ability, the will and the imagination to plan and build our future city together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has changed the way we live.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We now spend more time in our homes and are more keenly aware of the state of our living environment and neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: All of us want to live in a well-maintained estate with convenient access to services and enjoy good, friendly relations with our neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Municipal Services Office, or MSO sees opportunities to help more Singaporeans achieve this vision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In its first phase, MSO has worked closely with 10 agencies and now 17 Town Councils to improve our feedback response time and resolve complex issues more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In its next phase, MSO will work with these partners to deliver high-quality, resident-centric services, pre-empt issues where possible and partner like-minded residents to build a better neighbourhood together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about the impact of COVID-19 on the delivery of municipal services and what MSO would do to address these challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Indeed, at the height of circuit breaker, many municipal tasks had to be de-prioritised due to the lack of available manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As we emerge stronger from these disruptions, we need to move away from a heavy reliance on manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One way to do that, as rightly pointed out by Ms Tin Pei Ling, is to leverage technology for predictive maintenance work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO and our partners are doubling down on such efforts, to spot issues – and resolve them – before they become a problem for residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, HDB is working with Town Councils to progressively install the Smart Lighting System in all estates, which monitors common area lighting points in real time, and automatically adjusts them in response to human motion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This, like other predictive capabilities undertaken by NParks in the management of greenery and parks, enables us to better predict potential faults, and undertake pre-emptive rectifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We look forward to the trial outcomes, and to supporting their scale-up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also need to address structural barriers that prevent us from providing better services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This model integrates municipal services that are already outsourced by Government agencies today around residents’ needs at the township level, rather than by agency and land boundaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we can more swiftly resolve municipal issues within the same town, such as connectivity-related infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we can provide services more efficiently, by streamlining operational processes and training workers to be multi-skilled, so that they can be flexibly deployed across job functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, workers inspecting for municipal infrastructure defects could also be trained to spot pest issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over time, more higher-skilled municipal jobs will be created for locals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This integration of services, alongside our harnessing of tech and data insights, will lead to better maintained neighbourhoods for our residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked how MSO was using technology to make providing feedback easier and more inclusive, and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked on the progress of the OneService Chatbot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we piloted the OneService Lite QR code reporting in Jurong-Clementi and Aljunied-Hougang Town Councils last year, so that residents can report issues without downloading an app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This year, we will expand it to more estates in Holland-Bukit Panjang and Sembawang Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, in our trial in Yuhua last year, some seniors shared that QR codes were more convenient than phone calls, as they did not need to wait to speak to the phone operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They asked if feedback reporting could be done in vernacular languages, which they are more familiar with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have taken in the feedback and will be starting a trial for OneService Lite reporting in Chinese, and later in Malay and Tamil as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we have made progress in developing the OneService chatbot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Residents can look forward to reporting cases on-the-go, via WhatsApp and Telegram in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is expected to improve as public trials continues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This conversational reporting format complements the OneService App’s more structured reporting format.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan commented on closing the loop on municipal feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some complex cases require extensive investigation or repair works, and we agree that cases should not be marked as “closed” when agencies have undertaken to handle them but have not completed their actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together, providing feedback will be even more convenient, inclusive, and integrated with our everyday lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Ms Nadia Samdin and Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about MSO’s effort to encourage greater neighbourliness, so that residents can live harmoniously alongside each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In October last year, MSO hosted an Emerging Stronger Conversation focusing on this exact topic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many participants hoped for neighbourhoods where neighbours know and talk to each other, are considerate and tolerant, and are able to work issues out amongst themselves, rather than just complain to the authorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the spirit of SG Together, we want to support residents in translating these and other worthy goals into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we will enhance the OneService app so that residents can look out for one another, especially those in need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is especially important during the pandemic, where residents may find themselves having fewer interactions with their usual social networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, residents can soon alert their neighbours in the same block to upcoming renovations with the “Happenings” feature, so that affected neighbours can plan around such inconveniences and find alternative spots to rest and work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have also used the What Say You? residents survey tool to support Town Councils in polling residents on neighbourhood renewal programmes and block paintings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We look forward to collaborating with Mr Baey Yam Keng Tampines Town Council team in using this tool to facilitate community decision making for the residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we will provide support and funds for residents to develop community solutions for issues within their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are doing this via the Love Our ‘Hood Initiative, with the support of MCCY and the Singapore Kindness Movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over 30 passionate participants in Mountbatten spent the last 2 months tapping on their ground knowledge to develop initiatives to tackle issues such as animal feeding and neighbour noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Residents in Bukit Gombak and Pioneer can also look forward to participating in Love Our ‘Hood initiatives at their neighbourhoods later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also sustain our support of the community through the now-formalised OneService Kakis Network, which comprises over 2,000 members of public and stakeholders we have worked with over the years, and bring these like-minded citizens together to spark off ideas with one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For our upcoming estates, HDB launched the new Designing for Life roadmap last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This sets out how HDB will plan and design both new and existing areas to provide a high-quality living environment that can better support residents’ overall health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As for our existing estates, we have many upgrading programmes to keep them in good condition, including the Home Improvement Programme at the block-level, the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme at the neighbourhood-level, and the Remaking Our Heartland Programme at the town-level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members raised queries on some of our block-level works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, Mr Lim Biow Chuan had concerns about spalling concrete in older blocks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As HDB flats age, there will be some natural wear and tear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More details on HIP II will be shared closer to its commencement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the Lift Upgrading Programme, or LUP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, we have provided direct lift access for the vast majority of HDB blocks, including by exercising flexibility for some blocks above the cost cap of $30,000 per household.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, for blocks where the costs are still too high, it would not be prudent to offer the LUP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Faisal Manap suggested a national programme for façade repairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The external walls of HDB blocks are common property under Town Councils’ management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are currently no plans for a new programme for façade repairs, as such issues can be addressed through regular maintenance by the Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To ensure that building façades are regularly inspected and promptly repaired, BCA has also introduced the Periodic Façade Inspection regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond these block-level works, at the wider neighbourhood- and town-level, we will continue to involve residents in revitalising our common spaces, to keep them vibrant and to foster a stronger sense of community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, residents can help shape the rejuvenation of their towns through the Remaking Our Heartland programme, or ROH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For the latest batch of ROH towns in Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Merah, Choa Chu Kang, and Queenstown, HDB gathered feedback through an online survey, and engaged more than 300 residents and Grassroot Leaders through Zoom focus group discussions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB will now study residents’ suggestions, and work with relevant agencies on the preliminary proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will then engage residents again to further develop the proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to review the design and implementation of our upgrading schemes to meet residents’ evolving needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our rejuvenation efforts extend to our neighbourhood commercial spaces as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Associate Professor Jamus Lim suggested converting the top floor of HDB’s multi-storey carparks to commercial use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These may not be very suitable for commercial facilities, as retailers usually prefer locations with good pedestrian flow and visibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Instead, the top decks of such carparks are typically landscaped and provided with recreational facilities like playgrounds, exercise areas, and community gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some can even be converted into urban farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such landscaping also helps to reduce the urban heat island effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Nonetheless, HDB makes sure to include enough commercial spaces in its estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most HDB residents can access commercial facilities within 400 metres of their homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB has also been working closely with heartland shops in their revitalisation and digitalisation efforts, which have become even more important amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: RetailerLink helps HDB retailers manage customer engagement and promotions, and analyse sales data; while ShopperLink allows shoppers to browse and purchase products from heartland shops, attend their events, and even chat with the shop staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together with MTI and MCI, we are also improving the Revitalisation of Shops framework to facilitate upgrading for heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB will continue to partner our heartland shops in their transformation journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through these various platforms and initiatives, residents can look forward to more opportunities to contribute ideas and efforts, as we work together to build a more caring and vibrant neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Chairman, before I conclude, please allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Municipal Services Office (MSO) will work with agencies, Town Councils and residents to build a better living environment together in the following ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will enable us to resolve the municipal issues more swiftly and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we will make feedback provision more convenient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, we piloted the OneService Lite QR code reporting in Jurong-Clementi and Aljunied-Hougang Town Councils, so that residents can report issues simply by scanning a QR code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This year, we will expand it to more estates in Holland-Bukit Panjang and Sembawang Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also provide support and funds for residents to develop community solutions for issues within their neighbourhoods via the Love Our 'Hood Initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the past two months, over 30 passionate participants in Mountbatten have helped to develop initiatives to tackle issues such as animal feeding and neighbour noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Residents in Bukit Gombak and Pioneer can also look forward to participating in Love Our 'Hood Initiative later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to work with HDB residents to rejuvenate our estates, through the Remaking Our Heartlands programme, and to revitalise our heartland shops through the Revitalisation of Shops framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us build lively and vibrant neighbourhoods together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: COVID-19 may have changed the way we live.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But it has also given us the opportunity – and renewed impetus – to build well-maintained, connected and caring neighbourhoods together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic has affected many Singaporeans, with the lower income and vulnerable among us especially hard-hit, for instance, in terms of jobs and income loss.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, the crisis has brought out the best in us.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We saw so many individuals and groups stepping forward to help others.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, groups of volunteers went out at night to befriend rough sleepers, distribute essentials and offer them shelter and assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government has also implemented extensive support to help lower income households bounce back stronger from these challenging times, including through the COVID-19 Budget measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also rolled out additional support for households living in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Late payment charges have also been suspended from April 2020 to March 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To Ms Carrie Tan’s suggestion on further rent waivers, I would like to assure her that the Government will continue providing targeted support to lower income households to cope with the impact of COVID-19, for example, via the Household Support Package announced during the Budget speech, as well as the COVID-19 Recovery Grant and Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Government agencies and community partners have also stepped up outreach to public rental households to offer assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB has sent out letters and SMSes to inform these households to approach HDB or Social Service Offices (SSOs) if they cannot afford their rent or need other financial assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB has existing guidelines to lower the rent for households who cannot afford their rent.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In 2020, about 4,000 public rental households were assisted with lower rents, including those who experienced a fall in income.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also continue to look for more ways to partner the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I attended one of HDB’s Emerging Stronger Conversations, or ESC, on enhancing housing support for vulnerable communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The participants shared many thoughtful suggestions, including suggestions to help large families and singles staying in rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are studying these suggestions, and welcome more ideas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, our efforts to support those staying in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many rental families I met have shared with me their hope to own a home and provide a better environment for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is also our hope for them to realise this aspiration, and we have various measures to support them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They can tap on generous grants for their flat purchase, such as the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant for First-Timer families and the Step-Up CPF Housing Grant for Second-Timer families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme helps Second-Timer families with young children in public rental to own a home again.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since June 2019, tenants who have made a downpayment for a new flat will not have their rent increased for the rest of their stay in rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They can put the savings towards their upcoming new homes or other needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They can also get one-to-one guidance on home ownership from HDB’s Home ownership Support Team, or we call it HST, which was established in December 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In the past year, HST has assisted 654 rental households.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
