text: Among them, 50 have booked flats, and 177 should be ready to apply for a flat in the next one to two years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB will also work closely with MSF and other partners under Community Link, or ComLink, to provide coordinated support to our rental families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One family who has moved from their rental flat to a new flat with HST’s support is Mr Irman, his wife and their three children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They were staying in a 1-room flat in Bedok since 2005.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Family Service Centre referred the family to HST in September 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HST guided Mr Irman and his wife closely, from understanding their housing budget and options, and applying for the flat, to key collection and settling into their new home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The family moved into their new 3-room flat in Bedok in June 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many rental families have already moved on to home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Another 2,000 are waiting for the flats that they have booked to be completed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about the supply of public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We currently have enough supply for households who need them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue building a small number of new rental flats to replace older blocks that are redeveloped, and gradually renew our stock of rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Designing our HDB blocks and neighbourhoods to be inclusive, where Singaporeans regardless of background live together and share common spaces, continues to be an important part of how we will build a stronger, more caring and more cohesive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Therefore, we will integrate new rental flats that HDB builds with sold flats in the same BTO projects, including in prime areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Where feasible, we will build them in the same blocks too.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The first such mixed block is located at Marsiling Greenview, which was completed in June 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Feedback from residents living in both rental and sold flats has been largely positive.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Chong Kee Hiong raised concerns about large families staying in public rental flats and asked if we can provide larger flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This was also discussed at the ESC I attended.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families with three or more persons living in a 1-room flat can approach HDB to transfer to a 2-room flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families that form two nuclei, such as families with children, parents and grandparents living together, can apply for another flat, and HDB will offer them a second rental flat in the same block where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the moment, we have a very limited supply of such flats, so we will only be able to offer the flats to a small number of families, based on the families’ circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, all families with children living in public rental flats will receive holistic support under ComLink to enable them to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, SSOs and community partners will engage the families to understand their needs, and connect them to programmes and services, such as employment assistance and childcare services.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As far as possible, we aim to uplift them so that they can eventually buy their own home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB’s HST is part of the ComLink network, to guide these families in budgeting and planning for home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Louis Ng shared concerns about the Joint Singles Scheme, or JSS, for public rental.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, some individuals face challenges in finding a flatmate to apply with, or in getting along with their flatmate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During the ESC, a few participants shared similar concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand their concerns and have been looking at ways to improve the JSS.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For older 1-room rental flats, HDB will install partitions at the tenants’ request.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB has installed partitions in about 530 existing rental flats so far.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Most single tenants are prepared to share a flat with a flatmate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Flat sharing enables companionship and mutual support, which is especially important for older tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It also allows us to help as many who need a public rental flat as possible, within our limited resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who have extenuating circumstances, such as medical conditions that make it unfeasible for them to share a flat, we are prepared to look into their requests to rent a flat alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In this new model, we will set aside a few floors in a few rental blocks and appoint social service agencies to manage the flats, including the flat-sharing arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The social service agencies will have better expertise to match singles of similar profiles, and to mediate disagreements that may arise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If necessary, they can also arrange for individuals to move to another flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The rents in this new model will be largely similar to the JSS rents, and tenants will be subject to the same eligibility conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB is working towards rolling out this pilot later this year and we will share more details when ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to support the housing needs of other vulnerable groups, such as single parents and divorcees, who Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Louis Chua spoke about.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Members who are aware of families or individuals who need assistance can refer them to HDB, and we will do our best to assist them, based on their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB has also been working closely with MSF, social service agencies, and community partners in the PEERS Network to assist rough sleepers and help them to move to more stable housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been expanding housing options for seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In December 2020, MND, HDB and MOH introduced the Community Care Apartments, or CCAs, a new assisted living typology that combines housing with care services and community living for seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This encouraging response validates the consultative approach that agencies took on in developing the concept, from the design of the units and communal spaces, to the services to provide.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Seniors, care-givers and healthcare professionals provided valuable feedback during Focus Group Discussions we held in 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, we added design features, such as the sliding partition to the flat, based on feedback that seniors appreciated the open layout but might desire more privacy at times.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Given the positive feedback and strong interest, we are studying plans for a second pilot site.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With the pilots, we will monitor how the flat design and care services promote the well-being of seniors, both physical and socio-emotional and support them to age in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These pilots will help us to further improve the housing and care options for our seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We continue to welcome feedback from seniors, as well as their care-givers and family members.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, let me now say a few words in Malay.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   The COVID-19 pandemic has affected the lives of many Singaporeans, especially the lower income and the vulnerable among us.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I was heartened to see the resilience shown by these families in coping with the impact on their jobs, health, and family life.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, our community spirit also became stronger.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many individuals and groups have stepped forward to help others in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government has also offered extensive support to help the lower income households.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, HDB provided rent rebates and rent reductions for households living in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If you know someone who needs further assistance, please ask them to approach HDB or the nearest Social Service Office (SSO).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the moment, we have a very limited supply of such three-room flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hence, we will only be able to offer these flats to a small number of families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The selection will be done jointly by HDB and MSF, based on the families’ circumstances and suitability.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As far as possible, we aim to uplift them so that they can be self-reliant and eventually own their own home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many young people have shared with me their aspiration to own a home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some already have a few children of their own, and they want to provide a better home environment for their families and children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Additionally, for families staying in public rental, the HDB’s Home ownership Support Team provides one-to-one guidance on how they can plan and work towards buying a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Working together with citizens, the community and various partners, we remain committed to strengthen our support for vulnerable citizens, uplift lower income families and meet the housing needs of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now elaborate on the Ministry's plans on how we are transforming the construction industry to create more jobs and opportunities for our firms and our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Xie Yao Quan spoke about the Construction Industry Transformation Map, or ITM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This has involved making use of sustainable technologies and designs, such as more energy-efficient systems to cool and ventilate our buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is driven by the adoption of innovative building approaches like Design for Manufacturing and Assembly, or DfMA for short, and digital technologies like Integrated Digital Delivery, or IDD.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: DfMA allows building components to be prefabricated off-site in automated facilities and subsequently assembled on-site.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This raises productivity, improves workmanship and reduces disamenities to residents near construction sites.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IDD connects the various parts of the building lifecycle together via a digital spine.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This facilitates coordination among project stakeholders which improves accuracy of design and planning and reduces abortive work downstream.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have built up IDD competencies in more than 150 firms through 48 demonstration projects over the last three years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: A good example is Techniques Air-conditioning & Engineering Pte Ltd, an SME specialising in the installation of mechanical services.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: When I spoke to them earlier, they shared they have tapped on BCA's Productivity Innovation Project, or PIP scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: They have switched over to a prefabricated mechanical, electrical and plumbing, or MEP system.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Techniques shared with me that onsite works involving the installation of pipes and ducts took about two to three weeks in the past.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Time was needed to erect the scaffolding, perform welding and insulation works and conduct regular tests on the installation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, with the use of prefabricated vertical riser modules, such works are done well within a single day onsite.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Techniques has also leveraged the Building Information Modelling (BIM) and automation through its use of computer numerical control, or CMC machines to raise productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Cutting instructions to the machines can be automatically generated from a 3D building model, allowing changes to be made quickly and accurately.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: What used to take one-and-a-half hours using manual templates can be done in just 15 minutes, and precision is much better than previously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Furthermore, Techniques shared with me that they have been able to remotely coordinate with other firms and reduce the number of workers required onsite, making it easier to adhere to safe management measures, especially during this period.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Without these earlier investments, many of our firms would have been more severely disrupted during the challenging COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As many Members, like Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Xiao Yao Quan and Ms Poh Li San have pointed out, although we have made good progress, we need to pick up the pace of transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are making a greater whole-of-nation push on environmental sustainability – with the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Built Environment sector plays an important role in achieving our vision of a greener and more sustainable Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There is also greater urgency to strengthen the resilience of our sector, particularly in reducing reliance on foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the near term, we expect our foreign manpower situation to remain in flux, while COVID-19 travel restrictions are still in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To alleviate the current labour shortage in the construction industry, we are working closely with MOM and MOH to progressively increase the number of incoming workers but in a safe way, to minimise the risks of COVID-19 transmission in our dormitories and into our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, we want to ensure that migrant workers who are already in Singapore can continue to work here if they choose to.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have invested significantly to keep them safe and they are familiar with our local work culture and environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In this respect, we are working closely with the Singapore Contractors Association Limited, or SCAL, to facilitate a change of employer for construction workers whose contracts have either expired or were terminated through the SCAL Manpower Exchange.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, even as we work closely with our firms to overcome near-term challenges, we recognise that COVID-19 has hastened the shift towards a manpower-lean approach to construction, not just in Singapore, but across many other countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Recently, a local subsidiary of a large Chinese construction firm shared with me that the Chinese construction industry is facing a labour crunch.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Imagine, even in one of the world's largest labour markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The median age of the parent company's few million workers in China is 46.5 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The managing director lamented to me that it was increasingly difficult to attract young people into the sector, even with competitive wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Even fewer of them wanted to come and work in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Like what we are doing in Singapore, the firm is ramping up its investments in DfMA automation and digitalisation in China so as to reduce its reliance on manpower and to build with sustainability in mind.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, these are long-term structural shifts confronting our Built Environment sector, accelerated by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the spirit of emerging stronger, we have to seize this window of opportunity to transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we will raise standards of sustainability and productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about the Green Building Masterplan and how we plan to curb building emissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Over the past year, BCA and the Singapore Green Building Council have engaged over 5,000 stakeholders, ranging from developers, consultants, builders, members of the public, especially our young people.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There is strong support for our Green Building agenda, and a collective desire to ramp up our efforts to combat climate change in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Green buildings reap net savings over their life-cycle, despite the higher upfront cost.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, a large office building of over 15 storeys can save around $300,000 in operating costs annually by achieving the Green Mark Platinum standard.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Additionally, we will update the Green Mark scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The scheme recognises buildings that pursue sustainability standards beyond the minimum requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As Mr Henry Kwek has pointed out, our Green Mark scheme is amongst the world’s leading green building certifications, and a go-to standard for green buildings in the tropics.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Green Mark scheme already encourages reduction of not just operational carbon, but also embodied carbon, through the use of low-carbon materials and sustainable construction.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek will also be pleased to know that it already promotes the use of natural ventilation as a passive strategy to cool buildings and improve energy savings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The revised scheme will raise energy performance standards and place greater emphasis on other aspects of sustainability, such as health and well-being, and how the buildings are designed for long-term maintainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We intend to trial these new standards from the second quarter of this year, and will take into account industry feedback before we implement the revised scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA will provide more details in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will also continue our efforts to green our existing stock of buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: An important step is to enhance data transparency on building energy performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Currently, we collect and publish the energy performance data of our commercial and institutional buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Going forward, we will identify all buildings in the data that we publish, beginning with commercial buildings from the second half of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will allow building owners to benchmark their buildings against others at no additional cost, and spur them to improve their energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also exploring other ways to encourage building owners to conduct energy audits and retrofit their buildings to improve energy performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to engage the industry and public to ensure that our plans remain relevant over time as we transition to a more sustainable, low carbon Built Environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Next, let me touch on raising productivity in our sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have seen good productivity outcomes from adopting DfMA and aim to make DfMA the default building method for larger projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under the Buildability framework, projects with Gross Floor Area or GFA of at least 5,000 sqm, are required to meet minimum Buildable Design Scores or B-scores through the adoption of labour-efficient designs and technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This means that, eventually, around 80% of the GFA of all projects submitted for approval will be subject to the higher minimum B-score.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA will consult the industry in the coming months before firming up the enhanced standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This move will help us achieve our target of 70% DfMA adoption by 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also working closely with the industry to step up our digitalisation and IDD efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As mentioned by Minister Indranee Rajah, the Digitalising Built Environment Alliance for Action or AfA has identified common data environment (CDE) data standards as a key enabler to drive digitalisation across the entire value chain.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The common data standards specify what information is required for a project and how it can be structured.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Wide adoption of these common standards will facilitate information flow across platforms and enable seamless collaboration amongst the various supply chain partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about the support we are providing to local SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: SMEs make up 98% of our construction firms and play a very critical role in our sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our firms, especially SMEs, can tap on the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF) for support to adopt productive technologies and develop their workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, the Productivity Innovation Project (PIP) scheme, helps to defray the costs of adopting DfMA and IDD technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Techniques Air-Conditioning & Engineering Pte Ltd, which I mentioned earlier, is a very good example.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will also continue to enhance co-funding support of 80% under the PIP scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage all firms to make full use of the CPCF to undertake productivity improvements.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek talked about the difficulty in encouraging Singaporeans to join the construction industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan also asked what types of new jobs in the sector that Singaporeans can look forward to.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is common to associate jobs in the construction sector with the "three Ds": "dirty, dangerous and demanding".

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, as part of this transformation effort, the industry has made strides in redesigning existing jobs and creating new and higher-skilled jobs with better working environments.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There are many exciting career pathways in areas such as Digital Delivery Management and Smart Facilities Management.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many of these job roles did not even exist a decade ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I recently met Mr Lee Kong Jian, a bright NTU graduate with a background in Civil Engineering.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He is working at an Integrated Construction and Prefabrication Hub (ICPH), operated by local contractor Soilbuild Construction Group.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Kong Jian is a DfMA engineer in ICPH.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: His day-to-day job, or day-to-day work, involves using various digital platforms to manage the prefabrication production and delivery of precast concrete components, optimising the process for efficiency while maintaining quality standards for his clients.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: His job will not be out of place in a high-tech manufacturing factory.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, think about it – creating good, exciting jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we are stepping up our efforts to attract local PMETs and more tech-savvy young Singaporeans to join the Built Environment sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Please take a look at it, there are many exciting job roles, for example, Digital Delivery Specialist, Logistics Supply Chain Planner and Environmental Specialist.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also investing in our local workforce to acquire the relevant skills in many areas, especially those that are in demand – green buildings, DfMA and IDD.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In September last year, we rolled out the Skills Framework for the Built Environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The framework promotes recognition of skills development to enhance career progression opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA is working with the various Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to align accreditation schemes with the various progression pathways and skill requirements for the various job roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to build a strong talent pipeline through our iBuildSG Scholarship and Sponsorship Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As of January 2021, we have awarded more than 3,600 scholarships and sponsorships to local students.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we are not just only focusing on new entrants into the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are taking pains and effort to upgrade our existing workforce as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I had the privilege of speaking to Ms Kartini, a 45-year-old lady who has been working as a 2D drafter at infrastructure consulting firm, AECOM Singapore, for the last 18 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With the support from her firm and her supervisor whom I spoke to as well, Ms Kartini enrolled in the Professional Conversion Programme, or PCP, for BIM Professionals to upgrade her skillsets for 3D drafting.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, Ms Kartini is redeployed as a BIM modeller at AECOM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: When I spoke to her, there was a palpable sense of satisfaction and pride in having achieved the skills upgrade.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: She shared with me that her children are very proud of her, and she was very proud of herself.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: She learnt valuable skills from 2D drafting to 3D modelling, and she shared that 3D modelling enabled them to troubleshoot problems early in the construction process compared to previous ways of doing things.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, we are bringing new entrants into the Built Environment sector by making the effort to train our local workforce and the existing workforce in new skills and new job roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I urge more firms to tap on these training programmes to upskill their mid-career staff to take on these roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government is committed to working hand in hand with our tripartite partners, industry associations, firms and unions to transform the Built Environment sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We envisage a high-tech and integrated construction eco-system, led by progressive local firms with a strong local core, poised to capture even more opportunities abroad as we transform our sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We hope, and I personally hope, that when we come to talk about jobs in the construction sector, we are no longer associating them with the "three Ds" of "dirty, dangerous and demanding", but a refreshed set of three Ds: desirable jobs, in-demand skills and dynamic careers, allowing us to tap on the imagination, passion and capabilities of our firms and Singaporeans to build a much greener, vibrant and sustainable Singapore for tomorrow.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I have one clarification for Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: For companies that are in the Built Environment who are on existing support schemes, if they actually have the intent to improve and invest on capabilities for the longer term, can they actually move from the existing schemes to the integrated GTS support and how should they go about that?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I do not believe any of the officeholders have addressed my proposals about the Temporary Development Levy (TDL).

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: First, I have asked whether the TDL applicants will discuss the split of the TDL between the landlord and the tenant; second, to give businesses a choice of temporary permission of between three and five years to align with typical commercial tenancy agreements; and third, to give deserving businesses rebates or deferments of their TDL if they need it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But just some background, the TDL framework, as had been our response to the Member's Parliamentary Question, I think, last month or the month before is something that we allow the landlord and the tenant to work out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And by and large, it is typically the business owner who will pay for the TDL.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of the duration, URA evaluates planning applications according to the planning intentions for the site, the area the site is situated in and the prevailing policies and guidelines for the proposals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, they can then realign contracts with existing business conditions through mutual agreement with counterparties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If they cannot reach agreement, then they can terminate it and unwind.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is the existing framework but let us look at the Member's specific proposal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I believe my cut on cat ownership in HDB flats was not answered but I assume the answer is still a "no" and, if it is still a "no", could I at least ask whether we can extend the current pilot in Chong Pang, where HDB residents are allowed to keep cats, to other constituencies?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I would volunteer my own constituency of Nee Soon East and, maybe, the Member of Parliament for Kembangan/Chai Chee will volunteer as well.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Again, I have to emphasise I remain neutral on this topic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I mean, my MND colleagues and I do not intend to play a cat-and-mouse game with the Member on this question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said previously, we are studying this issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to enable pet ownership in a responsible way but we also have to balance a couple of other considerations, including municipal as well as neighbourhood issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I just have a quick follow-up question for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I appreciate her response that commercial facilities may require footfall and, hence, some commercial facilities may not be attractive on upper floors of MSCPs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But, surely, a cafe or a laundromat on the upper decks of an MSCP that is just downstairs of a flat would really be attractive to someone, compared to one located 400 m away.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I have many residents that shared that they miss the convenience of having a mama shop just downstairs of their place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, in the spirit of pilot suggestions, I wonder if HDB would consider a pilot, perhaps in Sengkang, for this kind of possibility of commercial spaces in MSCPs.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As shared, where we place the commercial facilities in any town would have to take into account the shops that have already been planned for and also in terms of the space that is proposed, whether, for instance, it was built for that purpose and, if it is not built for that purpose, what kind of modifications would be required in order to achieve that purpose.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But what I have shared would be the general factors for consideration.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: One is for Senior Minister Sim Ann – Madam, please do not go away yet.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Just wanted to ask about the spalling concrete.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: When the residents complained about spalling concrete, it is like going to drop onto their head and, frequently, they want a solution fast.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: But the reality is that when we complained to HDB about the spalling concrete, they take a while for someone to come, inspect the place, then arrange for a contractor to come.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: In the meanwhile, the resident says that "Hey, look, you know, this thing is going to drop on my head.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: It is gonna to injure me and it is going to hurt me any time." So, is there any way that we can ask HDB to do a more comprehensive programme whereby we can try to put a stop to the issue of spalling concrete?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: The second clarification that I require is from Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I understand the proposal to have a partition in the 1-room flat.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: But may I ask the Minister of State what is the response of residents to this 1-room flat being partitioned?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Because at the end of the day, the residents who share a 1-room flat have to share toilets, they have got to share the kitchen as well, and we are not going to be able to say that "Look, you know, my soap is here and the shampoo is somewhere else." They have to share facilities.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Frequently, the feedback that I get is that they are unhappy about having to share and that is why some of them then moved out from the flat and sleep in the void deck.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: So, is that really the solution that we want?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: So, perhaps Minister of State can clarify that for me.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for the question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have shared in my speech, we have built new rental flats with partition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, we have received requests to do it at the older rental flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One point to note is that a majority of those who live in rental flats, especially under the JSS, they are able to live together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, there are times that individuals may not be able to live together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We constantly look at it, engage them and, at the same time, we explore areas where we can help to improve the condition or privacy provided.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, what we found is that what they need are places where they can rest with privacy and also, at the same time, are able to use the facilities available in the flat.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, using of the toilet, using of the kitchen, I think they are okay sharing it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But, essentially, what we found is that, which I shared earlier, when they want to rest, they want to sleep, I think what is important is they want to have their private space in there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: On our part, we will continue to look at avenues to improve it, not only within the rental flats but also outside the rental flats, which we have done for some, and we find that these are areas where the tenants feel and appreciate it, and we will not stop there.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I have a supplementary question for Minister of State Tan Kiat How regarding R&D and its role within the context of the Industry Transformation Map.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Now, I am very heartened to hear that tremendous resources have been put into the adoption of DfMA, IDD and the Green Plan.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But R&D is also a key part for us to achieve industry transformation beyond adoption.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Both the research as well as the development, which is more like localisation of international technology within the Singapore context, within our Singapore realities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: So, can the Minister of State share on how are we promoting R&D and technology pilots within the context of industry transformation?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his question.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As Minister Desmond Lee has pointed earlier in his speech, investing in innovation to spur growth and transformation is an important part of building a resilient Built Environment sector and we will continue to invest in R&D and innovation to drive growth for our sector, particularly in transformative technologies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: A key focus area is the development of technologies that will help us to build faster, safer and using less manpower.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I think Minister Indranee Rajah spoke about the Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme, and we support R&D efforts through that programme on advanced construction techniques, particularly for robotics, automation, 3D concrete printing and digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are some of the areas, I think, Member Ms Poh Li San spoke about just now in her cut.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Minister Indranee Rajah spoke about the noise cancellation window just now.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And let me give another example of some of the innovation and R&D work that our colleagues have been doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is called the anti-sway device – "sway" is S-W-A-Y; not "suay" for bad luck in Hokkien!

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: HDB and BCA are collaborating with researchers from NUS, A*STAR SIMTech and industry partners, such as Precast Concrete and Dragages to develop an anti-sway device to stabilise the movement of prefabricated pre-finished volumetric construction, or PPVC modules during hoisting operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The anti-sway device which will be fitted on cranes and hooked onto the PPVC modules includes a self-balancing system that reduces the manpower required to manually stabilise the modules.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It does not sound as exciting compared to the noise cancellation windows, but an important investment in R&D in the Built Environment sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Just one example to share with the Member.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: However, the Member also pointed out a very important point about not just R&D but translating it into use on the ground, working together with our private sector partners and our companies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To achieve meaningful impact, we are stepping up efforts to support deployment of innovative urban solutions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is achieved by providing a convenient one-stop service for submission of test-bedding proposals and reducing regulatory burden on firms.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Living Lab Framework will be supported by the existing inter-agency Building Innovation Panel to facilitate multi-agency regulatory clearances for more complex solutions, and I encourage more firms to tap on this Living Lab Framework to come forward with good proposals.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think the Minister talked about the aspirations of home ownership and meeting them.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But at the same time, given the current socio-economic trends, I think rentals in a sharing economy, this is also something which is gaining traction amongst younger Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, again, to quote Westlife, a "world of our own" may mean not just owned flats but also rental flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Is MND considering expanding the supply of rental flats to meet this demographic trend and also the demands of the public rental scheme?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When you talk about rental flats, a lot of us in this House relate to rental housing for lower income households.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While waiting for the BTO flat to be completed, they are able to access these flats and rent a flat for those few years at subsidised rates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There was initially slow, low interest at first, but it has become an option of interest to many young couples who are currently living with parents – they are now able to live together and set up their own home in with their own privacy for those few years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I think the Member makes a broader point which is a diversity of housing options on the longer term basis, for people who may feel that home ownership is not for them or not for them at that point in time, and they would prefer to rent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is a rental market out there for people to rent smaller units, both in the private market, as well as HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB continues to look at various housing options.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To provide diversity, we have over the years, provided even more choice in terms of length of lease, in terms of the social accompaniments  to housing, in relation to rental for young couples, in relation to rental housing for the lower income.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, we continuously look at the aspirations of Singaporeans and see how we can provide the support for those aspirations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Speaker, thank you for allowing me to make the cut so late in the day, but I would like to ask the Minister regarding my cut earlier, with regard to the EIP question, I suggested an EIP price harmonisation grant for the minority residents who are affected by the EIP, so that we can reduce any indirect negative market effects of the EIP, and also encourage them to sell their flats at a lower price to buyers of the same ethnic group.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The reason why I asked is because I have been approached by a number of my residents who either Malay, Eurasian or Indian who are elderly and middle-aged and they want to downgrade.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And they are having difficulty selling their flats, waiting up to six to nine months even.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I am aware that on a case-by-case basis, the Minister mentioned just now, time extensions, case-by-case basis, and look at them intensely on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But in principle, is MND looking for any sort of help or assistance to reduce, narrow some of these potential economic inequalities that may arise from the EIP?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are grateful that Singaporeans, all these decades, have been supportive of multi-culturalism and of the different institutions that we put in place in order to act as a bulwark to protect Singapore and to keep Singapore cohesive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, we are always reviewing our policies, looking at how, for institutions, including one as important as EIP, we can continue to find new ways and ideas so that public support continues to be behind such important institutions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: I also thank Minister Desmond Lee's sharing of the Singapore Green Building Masterplan's targets to meet the 80-80-80 goals.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: However, I believe my question on how we can ensure that property prices for our public housing can remain affordable inclusive and livable, may not have been answered.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: How can we do that while incorporating all these very ideal, new building requirements?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, accessible and affordable and inclusive housing in our HDB estates is a very important objective of the Housing and Development Board.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The efforts to transform and upgrade our Built Environment sector should not impact upon the pricing approach for HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I explained quite recently in this House, how HDB prices its flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We look at the market value of the flat based on its attributes as well as recent resales around the estate, and then make adjustments for the attributes of the flat, and then apply the subsidies in order to bring it to the affordable level.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank all the Members who have spoken in the MND COS.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: As we can all appreciate the work that MND deals with is both broad and complex, as it touches every person's lives on a daily basis, and more importantly throughout their entire life stage.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: So, I think from housing to workplaces, the construction industry, trees, animals and land use.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: There is always a constant need for us to tightly balance this, between demand as well as availability.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: And at the same time, we have to reimagine the city of the future.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: So, for that, I would like to express my sincere thanks to Minister Desmond Lee, Second Minister Indranee Rajah, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, Minister of State Faishal, Minister of State Tan, and especially, the hardworking team from the MND family.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: And with that Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw amendment.
